passages.text: How the Lord has covered the Daughter of Zion with the cloud of His anger! He has cast the glory of Israel from heaven to earth. He has abandoned His footstool in the day of His anger.
passages.sermon:
The Lord became angry.
He showed His anger against the people of Jerusalem.
Jerusalem is called the Daughter of Zion.
The Lord covered the Daughter of Zion with a cloud of His anger.
He threw down the glory of Israel from heaven to earth.
He did not remember His footstool when He was angry.
The footstool means the place where God’s presence rested among His people.
God turned away from Jerusalem in the day of His anger.
passages.original: אֵיכָה֩ יָעִ֨יב בְּאַפּ֤וֹ׀ אֲדֹנָי֙ אֶת־ בַּת־ צִיּ֔וֹן הִשְׁלִ֤יךְ מִשָּׁמַ֙יִם֙ אֶ֔רֶץ תִּפְאֶ֖רֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְלֹא־ זָכַ֥ר הֲדֹם־ רַגְלָ֖יו בְּי֥וֹם אַפּֽוֹ׃ס

passages.text: Without pity the Lord has swallowed up all the dwellings of Jacob. In His wrath He has demolished the fortified cities of the Daughter of Judah. He brought to the ground and defiled her kingdom and its princes.
passages.sermon:
The Lord acted without pity.
The Lord swallowed up all the dwellings of Jacob.
The Lord acted in wrath.
The Lord demolished the fortified cities of the Daughter of Judah.
The Lord brought her kingdom to the ground.
The Lord defiled her kingdom and its princes.
passages.original: בִּלַּ֨ע אֲדֹנָ֜י לֹא חָמַ֗ל אֵ֚ת כָּל־ נְא֣וֹת יַעֲקֹ֔ב הָרַ֧ס בְּעֶבְרָת֛וֹ מִבְצְרֵ֥י בַת־ יְהוּדָ֖ה הִגִּ֣יעַ לָאָ֑רֶץ חִלֵּ֥ל מַמְלָכָ֖ה וְשָׂרֶֽיהָ׃ס

passages.text: In fierce anger He has cut off every horn of Israel and withdrawn His right hand at the approach of the enemy. He has burned in Jacob like a flaming fire that consumes everything around it.
passages.sermon:
The Lord acted in fierce anger.
He cut off every horn of Israel.
He withdrew His right hand when the enemy came near.
He burned in Jacob like a flaming fire.
This fire consumed everything around it.
passages.original: גָּדַ֣ע בָּֽחֳרִי אַ֗ף כֹּ֚ל קֶ֣רֶן יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הֵשִׁ֥יב אָח֛וֹר יְמִינ֖וֹ מִפְּנֵ֣י אוֹיֵ֑ב וַיִּבְעַ֤ר בְּיַעֲקֹב֙ כְּאֵ֣שׁ לֶֽהָבָ֔ה אָכְלָ֖ה סָבִֽיב׃ס

passages.text: He has bent His bow like an enemy; His right hand is positioned. Like a foe He has killed all who were pleasing to the eye; He has poured out His wrath like fire on the tent of the Daughter of Zion.
passages.sermon:
The Lord acts with anger and judgment.
He bends His bow like an enemy.
He stands with His right hand ready, like a foe.
He kills everyone who is precious and pleasing to see.
He pours out His wrath like fire.
His anger falls on the tent of the Daughter of Zion.
passages.original: דָּרַ֨ךְ קַשְׁתּ֜וֹ כְּאוֹיֵ֗ב נִצָּ֤ב יְמִינוֹ֙ כְּצָ֔ר וַֽיַּהֲרֹ֔ג כֹּ֖ל מַחֲמַדֵּי־ עָ֑יִן בְּאֹ֙הֶל֙ בַּת־ צִיּ֔וֹן שָׁפַ֥ךְ כָּאֵ֖שׁ חֲמָתֽוֹ׃ס

passages.text: The Lord is like an enemy; He has swallowed up Israel. He has swallowed up all her palaces and destroyed her strongholds. He has multiplied mourning and lamentation for the Daughter of Judah.
passages.sermon:
The Lord acted like an enemy.
The Lord swallowed up Israel.
The Lord swallowed up all Israel’s palaces.
The Lord destroyed Israel’s strongholds.
The Lord increased mourning for the people of Judah.
The Lord increased lamentation for the people of Judah.
passages.original: הָיָ֨ה אֲדֹנָ֤י׀ כְּאוֹיֵב֙ בִּלַּ֣ע יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בִּלַּע֙ כָּל־ אַרְמְנוֹתֶ֔יהָ שִׁחֵ֖ת מִבְצָרָ֑יו וַיֶּ֙רֶב֙ בְּבַת־ יְהוּדָ֔ה תַּאֲנִיָּ֖ה וַאֲנִיָּֽה׃ס

passages.text: He has laid waste His tabernacle like a garden booth; He has destroyed His place of meeting. The LORD has made Zion forget her appointed feasts and Sabbaths. In His fierce anger He has despised both king and priest.
passages.sermon:
The LORD acted in anger.
He destroyed His tabernacle.
He made it like a temporary shelter in a garden.
He ruined His place of meeting.
The LORD caused Zion to forget her appointed feasts.
He caused Zion to forget her Sabbaths.
The LORD showed fierce anger.
He despised the king.
He despised the priest.
passages.original: וַיַּחְמֹ֤ס כַּגַּן֙ שֻׂכּ֔וֹ שִׁחֵ֖ת מוֹעֲד֑וֹ שִׁכַּ֨ח יְהוָ֤ה׀ בְּצִיּוֹן֙ מוֹעֵ֣ד וְשַׁבָּ֔ת וַיִּנְאַ֥ץ בְּזַֽעַם־ אַפּ֖וֹ מֶ֥לֶךְ וְכֹהֵֽן׃ס

passages.text: The Lord has rejected His altar; He has abandoned His sanctuary; He has delivered the walls of her palaces into the hand of the enemy. They have raised a shout in the house of the LORD as on the day of an appointed feast.
passages.sermon:
The Lord is the God of Israel.
The Lord has rejected His altar.
The Lord has abandoned His sanctuary.
The Lord has given the walls of Israel’s palaces to the enemy.
The enemy has entered the house of the Lord.
The enemy has shouted in the house of the Lord.
Their shout is loud, like the shout on a feast day.
passages.original: זָנַ֨ח אֲדֹנָ֤י׀ מִזְבְּחוֹ֙ נִאֵ֣ר מִקְדָּשׁ֔וֹ הִסְגִּיר֙ בְּיַד־ אוֹיֵ֔ב חוֹמֹ֖ת אַרְמְנוֹתֶ֑יהָ ק֛וֹל נָתְנ֥וּ בְּבֵית־ יְהוָ֖ה כְּי֥וֹם מוֹעֵֽד׃ס

passages.text: The LORD determined to destroy the wall of the Daughter of Zion. He stretched out a measuring line and did not withdraw His hand from destroying. He made the ramparts and walls lament; together they waste away.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD decided to destroy the wall of the Daughter of Zion.
The Daughter of Zion is Jerusalem.
The LORD stretched out a measuring line.
He did not pull back His hand from destroying.
The LORD caused the ramparts to mourn.
He caused the walls to mourn.
The ramparts and the walls waste away together.
passages.original: חָשַׁ֨ב יְהוָ֤ה׀ לְהַשְׁחִית֙ חוֹמַ֣ת בַּת־ צִיּ֔וֹן נָ֣טָה קָ֔ו לֹא־ הֵשִׁ֥יב יָד֖וֹ מִבַּלֵּ֑עַ וַיַּֽאֲבֶל־ חֵ֥ל וְחוֹמָ֖ה יַחְדָּ֥ו אֻמְלָֽלוּ׃ס

passages.text: Her gates have sunk into the ground; He has destroyed and shattered their bars. Her king and her princes are exiled among the nations, the law is no more, and even her prophets find no vision from the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The city’s gates have sunk into the ground.
The Lord has destroyed the gates.
He has shattered their bars.
The city’s king is gone.
Her princes are gone.
They live among foreign nations.
The law does not remain in the city.
Her prophets do not see visions from the Lord.
passages.original: טָבְע֤וּ בָאָ֙רֶץ֙ שְׁעָרֶ֔יהָ אִבַּ֥ד וְשִׁבַּ֖ר בְּרִיחֶ֑יהָ מַלְכָּ֨הּ וְשָׂרֶ֤יהָ בַגּוֹיִם֙ אֵ֣ין תּוֹרָ֔ה גַּם־ נְבִיאֶ֕יהָ לֹא־ מָצְא֥וּ חָז֖וֹן מֵיְהוָֽה׃ס

passages.text: The elders of the Daughter of Zion sit on the ground in silence. They have thrown dust on their heads and put on sackcloth. The young women of Jerusalem have bowed their heads to the ground.
passages.sermon:
The elders of the people of Zion sit on the ground.
They remain silent.
They are elders.
They belong to the Daughter of Zion.
They throw dust on their heads.
They put on sackcloth.
The young women of Jerusalem bow their heads to the ground.
They are young women.
They belong to Jerusalem.
passages.original: יֵשְׁב֨וּ לָאָ֤רֶץ יִדְּמוּ֙ זִקְנֵ֣י בַת־ צִיּ֔וֹן הֶֽעֱל֤וּ עָפָר֙ עַל־ רֹאשָׁ֔ם חָגְר֖וּ שַׂקִּ֑ים הוֹרִ֤ידוּ לָאָ֙רֶץ֙ רֹאשָׁ֔ן בְּתוּלֹ֖ת יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃ס

passages.text: My eyes fail from weeping; I am churning within. My heart is poured out in grief over the destruction of the daughter of my people, because children and infants faint in the streets of the city.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is a prophet of God.
The prophet weeps for his people.
His eyes are exhausted from crying.
His inner being is in turmoil.
His heart is poured out in grief.
He mourns the destruction of the daughter of his people.
Children faint in the city streets.
Infants collapse in the city streets.
This suffering causes the prophet deep sorrow.
passages.original: כָּל֨וּ בַדְּמָע֤וֹת עֵינַי֙ חֳמַרְמְר֣וּ מֵעַ֔י נִשְׁפַּ֤ךְ לָאָ֙רֶץ֙ כְּבֵדִ֔י עַל־ שֶׁ֖בֶר בַּת־ עַמִּ֑י בֵּֽעָטֵ֤ף עוֹלֵל֙ וְיוֹנֵ֔ק בִּרְחֹב֖וֹת קִרְיָֽה׃ס

passages.text: They cry out to their mothers: “Where is the grain and wine?” as they faint like the wounded in the streets of the city, as their lives fade away in the arms of their mothers.
passages.sermon:
Children speak to their mothers.
They say, “Where is the grain?
Where is the wine?”
Children grow weak in the city streets.
They faint like wounded people.
Their lives slip away in their mothers’ arms.
passages.original: לְאִמֹּתָם֙ יֹֽאמְר֔וּ אַיֵּ֖ה דָּגָ֣ן וָיָ֑יִן בְּהִֽתְעַטְּפָ֤ם כֶּֽחָלָל֙ בִּרְחֹב֣וֹת עִ֔יר בְּהִשְׁתַּפֵּ֣ךְ נַפְשָׁ֔ם אֶל־ חֵ֖יק אִמֹּתָֽם׃ס

passages.text: What can I say for you? To what can I compare you, O Daughter of Jerusalem? To what can I liken you, that I may console you, O Virgin Daughter of Zion? For your wound is as deep as the sea. Who can ever heal you?
passages.sermon:
Jerusalem is in great distress.
Jerusalem is called the Daughter of Jerusalem and the Virgin Daughter of Zion.
I do not know what to say to comfort you.
I do not know what to compare you to.
I do not know what to liken you to, so that I might console you.
Your wound is very great.
Your wound is as deep as the sea.
No one can heal you.
passages.original: מָֽה־ אֲעִידֵ֞ךְ מָ֣ה אֲדַמֶּה־ לָּ֗ךְ הַבַּת֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם מָ֤ה אַשְׁוֶה־ לָּךְ֙ וַאֲנַֽחֲמֵ֔ךְ בְּתוּלַ֖ת בַּת־ צִיּ֑וֹן כִּֽי־ גָד֥וֹל כַּיָּ֛ם שִׁבְרֵ֖ךְ מִ֥י יִרְפָּא־ לָֽךְ׃ס

passages.text: The visions of your prophets were empty and deceptive; they did not expose your guilt to ward off your captivity. The burdens they envisioned for you were empty and misleading.
passages.sermon:
Your prophets saw visions for you.
Their visions were empty.
Their visions were deceptive.
They did not reveal your guilt.
They did not warn you about your sins.
They did not help you avoid captivity.
They gave you burdens that were empty.
They gave you messages that misled you.
passages.original: נְבִיאַ֗יִךְ חָ֤זוּ לָךְ֙ שָׁ֣וְא וְתָפֵ֔ל וְלֹֽא־ גִלּ֥וּ עַל־ עֲוֺנֵ֖ךְ לְהָשִׁ֣יב שְׁבִיתֵךְ וַיֶּ֣חֱזוּ לָ֔ךְ מַשְׂא֥וֹת שָׁ֖וְא וּמַדּוּחִֽים׃ס

passages.text: All who pass by clap their hands at you in scorn. They hiss and shake their heads at the Daughter of Jerusalem: “Is this the city that was called the perfection of beauty, the joy of all the earth?”
passages.sermon:
The Daughter of Jerusalem is the city of Jerusalem.
All who pass by see Jerusalem.
They clap their hands at Jerusalem in scorn.
They hiss at Jerusalem.
They shake their heads at Jerusalem.
They say, “Is this the city?”
They remember that people once called Jerusalem the perfection of beauty.
They remember that people once called Jerusalem the joy of all the earth.
passages.original: סָֽפְק֨וּ עָלַ֤יִךְ כַּפַּ֙יִם֙ כָּל־ עֹ֣בְרֵי דֶ֔רֶךְ שָֽׁרְקוּ֙ וַיָּנִ֣עוּ רֹאשָׁ֔ם עַל־ בַּ֖ת יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם הֲזֹ֣את הָעִ֗יר שֶׁיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ כְּלִ֣ילַת יֹ֔פִי מָשׂ֖וֹשׂ לְכָל־ הָאָֽרֶץ׃ס

passages.text: All your enemies open their mouths against you. They hiss and gnash their teeth, saying, “We have swallowed her up. This is the day for which we have waited. We have lived to see it!”
passages.sermon:
Your enemies act with hatred toward you.
They open their mouths against you.
They hiss at you.
They gnash their teeth at you.
They say, “We have swallowed her up.”
They say, “This is the day we have waited for.”
They say, “We have found it.”
They say, “We have seen it.”
passages.original: פָּצ֨וּ עָלַ֤יִךְ פִּיהֶם֙ כָּל־ א֣וֹיְבַ֔יִךְ שָֽׁרְקוּ֙ וַיַּֽחַרְקוּ־ שֵׁ֔ן אָמְר֖וּ בִּלָּ֑עְנוּ אַ֣ךְ זֶ֥ה הַיּ֛וֹם שֶׁקִּוִּינֻ֖הוּ מָצָ֥אנוּ רָאִֽינוּ׃ס

passages.text: The LORD has done what He planned; He has accomplished His decree, which He ordained in days of old; He has overthrown you without pity. He has let the enemy gloat over you and exalted the horn of your foes.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD made a plan long ago.
The LORD decided what would happen to Jerusalem.
The LORD gave His command in ancient times.
The LORD has now done what He planned.
The LORD has carried out His word.
The LORD has destroyed Jerusalem.
The LORD did not show pity.
The LORD let your enemy rejoice over you.
The LORD let your foes become strong.
passages.original: עָשָׂ֨ה יְהוָ֜ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר זָמָ֗ם בִּצַּ֤ע אֶמְרָתוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוָּ֣ה מִֽימֵי־ קֶ֔דֶם הָרַ֖ס וְלֹ֣א חָמָ֑ל וַיְשַׂמַּ֤ח עָלַ֙יִךְ֙ אוֹיֵ֔ב הֵרִ֖ים קֶ֥רֶן צָרָֽיִךְ׃ס

passages.text: The hearts of the people cry out to the Lord. O wall of the Daughter of Zion, let your tears run down like a river day and night. Give yourself no relief, and your eyes no rest.
passages.sermon:
The people of Jerusalem suffer greatly.
Their hearts cry out to the Lord.
The city is called the Daughter of Zion.
The wall of the city stands as a witness.
O wall of the Daughter of Zion, let your tears flow like a river.
Let your tears run day and night.
Do not give yourself relief.
Do not let your eyes rest.
passages.original: צָעַ֥ק לִבָּ֖ם אֶל־ אֲדֹנָ֑י חוֹמַ֣ת בַּת־ צִ֠יּוֹן הוֹרִ֨ידִי כַנַּ֤חַל דִּמְעָה֙ יוֹמָ֣ם וָלַ֔יְלָה אַֽל־ תִּתְּנִ֤י פוּגַת֙ לָ֔ךְ אַל־ תִּדֹּ֖ם בַּת־ עֵינֵֽךְ׃ס

passages.text: Arise, cry out in the night from the first watch of the night. Pour out your heart like water in the presence of the Lord. Lift up your hands to Him for the lives of your children who are fainting from hunger on the corner of every street.
passages.sermon:
The Lord is the God of Israel.
He sees the suffering of His people.
You, people of Zion, are in distress.
Get up in the night.
Cry out loudly.
Begin at the first watch of the night.
Pour out your heart like water.
Do this before the Lord.
Lift up your hands to God.
Pray for your children.
Your children are weak with hunger.
They faint on every street corner.
passages.original: ק֣וּמִי׀ רֹ֣נִּי בַלַּיִל לְרֹאשׁ֙ אַשְׁמֻר֔וֹת שִׁפְכִ֤י כַמַּ֙יִם֙ לִבֵּ֔ךְ נֹ֖כַח פְּנֵ֣י אֲדֹנָ֑י שְׂאִ֧י אֵלָ֣יו כַּפַּ֗יִךְ עַל־ נֶ֙פֶשׁ֙ עֽוֹלָלַ֔יִךְ הָעֲטוּפִ֥ים בְּרָעָ֖ב בְּרֹ֥אשׁ כָּל־ חוּצֽוֹת׃ס

passages.text: Look, O LORD, and consider: Whom have You ever treated like this? Should women eat their offspring, the infants they have nurtured? Should priests and prophets be killed in the sanctuary of the Lord?
passages.sermon:
The people of Jerusalem speak to the Lord.
They ask God to look at their suffering.
They ask God to see what has happened to them.
They say, “Lord, whom have You ever treated like this?”
They ask, “Should women eat their own children?”
They mean the infants they have cared for and raised.
They ask, “Should priests and prophets be killed?”
They say these priests and prophets die in the Lord’s sanctuary.
passages.original: רְאֵ֤ה יְהוָה֙ וְֽהַבִּ֔יטָה לְמִ֖י עוֹלַ֣לְתָּ כֹּ֑ה אִם־ תֹּאכַ֨לְנָה נָשִׁ֤ים פִּרְיָם֙ עֹלֲלֵ֣י טִפֻּחִ֔ים אִם־ יֵהָרֵ֛ג בְּמִקְדַּ֥שׁ אֲדֹנָ֖י כֹּהֵ֥ן וְנָבִֽיא׃ס

passages.text: Both young and old lie together in the dust of the streets. My young men and maidens have fallen by the sword. You have slain them in the day of Your anger; You have slaughtered them without compassion.
passages.sermon:
Young people lie in the streets.
Old people lie in the streets.
They lie together in the dust.
My young men have fallen by the sword.
My maidens have fallen by the sword.
You killed them in Your anger.
You slaughtered them without showing compassion.
passages.original: שָׁכְב֨וּ לָאָ֤רֶץ חוּצוֹת֙ נַ֣עַר וְזָקֵ֔ן בְּתוּלֹתַ֥י וּבַחוּרַ֖י נָפְל֣וּ בֶחָ֑רֶב הָרַ֙גְתָּ֙ בְּי֣וֹם אַפֶּ֔ךָ טָבַ֖חְתָּ לֹ֥א חָמָֽלְתָּ׃ס

passages.text: You summoned my attackers on every side, as for the day of an appointed feast. In the day of the LORD’s anger no one escaped or survived; my enemy has destroyed those I nurtured and reared.
passages.sermon:
God summoned my attackers from every direction.
He called them as if He was calling people to a special feast.
This happened on the day of the LORD’s anger.
On that day, no one escaped.
No one survived.
My enemy destroyed everyone I had cared for.
My enemy destroyed everyone I had raised.
passages.original: תִּקְרָא֩ כְי֨וֹם מוֹעֵ֤ד מְגוּרַי֙ מִסָּבִ֔יב וְלֹ֥א הָיָ֛ה בְּי֥וֹם אַף־ יְהוָ֖ה פָּלִ֣יט וְשָׂרִ֑יד אֲשֶׁר־ טִפַּ֥חְתִּי וְרִבִּ֖יתִי אֹיְבִ֥י כִלָּֽם׃פ
